title: Posterior predictive counts for LZ's next release: P(0), P(1), P(>=2) high-energy events under the corpus posterior
question: Given P027's model-marginalised posterior, P061's hypothesis weights, P038's edge acceptance, P068's halo band and P034's seasonal PDFs, what is the posterior predictive distribution of high-energy NR-band events (200-270 keV; 55-270 keV; 55-420 keV with a 1000 phd edge) in LZ's next 1.0/2.8/5.6/10 t yr, and what Bayes-factor update does each outcome (0, 1, >=2 events; two events at various energies) produce?
headline_result: Under the corpus DM posterior LZ's next 2.8 t yr holds >=1 event in 200-270 keV with probability 0.25 (0.50 in 55-270 keV) vs 5.6e-4 for background; a new band event gives BF >= 300 against modelled/one-off backgrounds but <= 1.5 against a steady LZ-specific unknown, so P(DM|event,N) stays at 0.014-0.029 for every count and only events in 270-420 or 55-200 keV move it (two extension events: P(DM) = 0.99)
model_or_mechanism: P027 per-model rate posteriors p(s|m) ∝ π(s) e^-s (1+ρs/b_H) W_m(s) under log-uniform/flat/Jeffreys priors, weighted by P027 posterior model weights; region ratios from P027/P008 spectra with 600 and 1000 phd erf edges (P038); seasonal factor of the release window from P034 time PDFs; P068 a1 and delta_max bands as multiplicative/effective-delta spread; 400k-draw Monte Carlo Poisson predictive; P061 hyper-prior (20k draws) three-hypothesis mixture with one-off/steady unknown (Exponential(1) rate); Bayes factors and posteriors per outcome and energy placement
confidence: medium - exact reproduction of the P027/P061 machinery and cross-checks against P027/P069/P038, but hypothesis weights, the unknown's predictive (f_trans, localisation) and the 55-125 keV background are corpus judgements
agent_tools: Read x22, Bash x20, Write x5, Edit x25, Skill x1 (dataviz)
software_and_packages: python 3.12.13; numpy 2.5.3; scipy 1.18.1 (stats.norm, special.erf/logsumexp/gammaln); pandas 3.0.5; matplotlib 3.11.2; common/lzcommon.py (imported); WimPyDD 2.0.4 via P027/P008/P038/P050 caches
